function.name: search_google
function.description: Performs a search query on Google and returns a list of URLs that match the search criteria. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

query.description: The search term to query on Google.

num_results.description: The maximum number of search results to return. The number must be a positive integer.

language.description: The language for the search results.

filter.description: A flag to filter explicit content in search results.

date_range.description: The date range for the search results in the format 'MM/DD/YYYY-MM/DD/YYYY'. If not specified, searches across all dates.

Here’s a quick snapshot of some of the most prominent vaccine manufacturers worldwide (as of 2026).  The list includes companies that produce COVID‑19 vaccines, routine childhood vaccines, and other specialty immunizations.

| # | Company | Headquarters | Notable Vaccines | Notes |
|---|---------|--------------|------------------|-------|
| 1 | **Pfizer‑BioNTech** | New York, USA / Mainz, Germany | BNT162b2 (Comirnaty) – mRNA COVID‑19 vaccine | First mRNA vaccine to receive WHO emergency use listing (EUL). |
| 2 | **Moderna** | Cambridge, USA | mRNA‑1273 (Spikevax) – mRNA COVID‑19 vaccine | Rapidly scaled up production during the pandemic. |
| 3 | **Johnson & Johnson (Janssen)** | New Brunswick, USA | Ad26.COV2.S – single‑dose adenovirus‑vector COVID‑19 vaccine | Also produces a range of routine vaccines (e.g., meningococcal). |
| 4 | **AstraZeneca** | Cambridge, UK | ChAdOx1 nCoV‑19 (Vaxzevria) – adenovirus‑vector COVID‑19 vaccine | Co‑developed with the University of Oxford. |
| 5 | **Novavax** | Gaithersburg, USA | NVX-CoV2373 – protein‑subunit COVID‑19 vaccine | Uses a recombinant spike protein platform. |
| 6 | **Sinovac Biotech** | Beijing, China | CoronaVac – inactivated COVID‑19 vaccine | One of the largest producers of inactivated vaccines. |
| 7 | **Sinopharm (Hepatitis B & COVID‑19)** | Beijing, China | BBIBP‑CorV – inactivated COVID‑19 vaccine | WHO EUL‑approved. |
| 8 | **Bharat Biotech** | Hyderabad, India | Covaxin – inactivated COVID‑19 vaccine | Co‑developed with the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR). |
| 9 | **COVAX (Global Alliance for Vaccines and Immunization)** | Geneva, Switzerland | Not a manufacturer, but coordinates procurement and distribution of vaccines from multiple manufacturers. | Works closely with WHO and Gavi. |
|10 | **Serum Institute of India** | Pune, India | Routine childhood vaccines (e.g., DTP, Hib, IPV) | Largest vaccine manufacturer by volume worldwide. |
|11 | **Sanofi Pasteur** | Lyon, France | Routine vaccines (e.g., influenza, HPV, meningococcal) | Global presence in both routine and pandemic vaccines. |
|12 | **GlaxoSmithKline (GSK) Vaccines** | Brentford, UK | Routine vaccines (e.g., influenza, HPV, rotavirus) | Strong focus on research‑intensive vaccine development. |
|13 | **Merck & Co. (MSD)** | Kenilworth, USA | Routine vaccines (e.g., HPV, influenza) | Known for its research‑driven approach. |
|14 | **Biontech (formerly BioNTech)** | Mainz, Germany | mRNA‑1273 – mRNA COVID‑19 vaccine (in partnership with Moderna) | Also developing other mRNA therapeutics. |
|15 | **CureVac** | Tübingen, Germany | CVnCoV – mRNA COVID‑19 vaccine (phase 3 trials) | Focus on self‑amplifying RNA platforms. |

### How to Use This List
- **Research**: If you’re looking into vaccine supply chains, this table gives you a starting point for which companies to investigate further.
- **Procurement**: For public health agencies, the list highlights key players for negotiating contracts or exploring new vaccine options.
- **Academic**: For students or researchers, the table can serve as a quick reference for vaccine technology platforms (mRNA, adenovirus vector, protein subunit, inactivated).

If you need deeper details—such as manufacturing capacities, geographic distribution of production sites, or recent clinical trial data—just let me know!
